sources.entry: DOMJudge - System for running a programming contest, like the ICPC regional and world championship programming contests. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-2.0/BSD-3-Clause/MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: DOMjudge is a jury system for running programming contests such as ICPC regional and world championships, and it can also run IOI-style partial-scoring contests.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes DOMjudge as a system for running programming contests, citing ICPC regional and world championship formats, and says it can also run IOI-style contests with partial scoring. It is a PHP web application (the README mentions a webapp directory with Composer and npm dependencies). Documentation lives in doc/manual as reStructuredText, with a prebuilt HTML version. The README points to a separate team interface and a wiki covering specific configurations and integrations. Installation details are in the manual rather than the README, which says stable releases are preferred over git clones. The README does not list specific features beyond these points.
use_cases: hosting an IOI-style contest with partial scoring
running a jury system for contest teams
how_to_run: Download a stable release tarball or daily snapshot (recommended over git clone)
Read the installation instructions in the doc/manual directory
For development from git: run `make dist` to generate the configure script and documentation, then follow the manual's Development section
notable: Designed for ICPC-style and IOI-style (partial scoring) programming contests
Includes the default validator from Kattis problemtools (MIT licensed)
Separate team interface, whose documentation is configured per local environment
Documentation is shipped in the repository and built from reStructuredText sources
caveats: Bootstrapping from git requires running make dist first, and the README calls this an advanced or development use case
The README notes that the online documentation reflects the latest stable release and may not match other versions
Team documentation needs the system to be configured first, since it embeds local settings
summary.license: GPL-2.0 (README states DOMjudge is free software under GPL v2 or later; the included validator is MIT, and the awesome-selfhosted listing also gives BSD-3-Clause for some components)
